proof_summary: Multiplicativity of the divisor sum first forces an even perfect number into the form \(n=2^kq\), where \(q=2^{k+1}-1\) is prime. Its proper divisors include the disjoint blocks \(\{2^i:0\le i\le k\}\) and \(\{q2^i:0\le i<k\}\); binary expansion of quotient and remainder modulo \(q\) (with a separate endpoint representation for \(n\)) realizes every sum from \(0\) through \(n\), while perfectness ensures no subset sum exceeds \(n\).
